chunks.arabic_text: عُيُونُ أَخْبَارِ الرِّضَا: عَن أَبِيهِ، عَن سَعْدٍ، عَن مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى، عَن زِيَادِ بْنِ مَرْوَانَ الْقَنْدِيِّ قَالَ

translations.en: Uyun Akhbar al-Ridha: From his father, from Sa'd, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ziyad ibn Marwan al-Qandi who said:

chunks.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ عَلَى أَبِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ وَعِنْدَهُ ابْنُهُ أَبُو الْحَسَنِ فَقَالَ لِي: يَا زِيَادُ هَذَا ابْنِي فُلَانٌ كِتَابُهُ كِتَابِي وَكَلَامُهُ كَلَامِي وَرَسُولُهُ رَسُولِي وَمَا قَالَ فَالْقَوْلُ قَوْلُهُ

translations.en: I entered to meet Abi Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and with him was his son Abu al-Hasan. He said to me: O Ziyad, this is my son so-and-so; his letter is my letter, his speech is my speech, his messenger is my messenger, and whatever he says, the ruling is what he says.

en.summary: This hadith from *Aynun al-Akhbar al-Rida* establishes the principle of *Nass* (designation) by explicitly linking Imam al-Hadi to his father, Imam al-Rida, affirming the continuity of authority. The Imam’s declaration that the son’s letter, speech, and messengership are identical to his own underscores the theological concept of the Imam as the infallible interpreter of divine law, a cornerstone of Shia jurisprudence. This specific narration serves as a critical proof for the legitimacy of the Imams' teachings during the period of relative concealment.
en.seo_question: What did Imam al-Rida say about the authority of his son Imam al-Hadi?

key_terms.الْقَوْلُ قَوْلُهُ: The ruling is what he says (binding authority)
